This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1988 for the relief of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
2.

The petition averments are briefly stated as follows:
SCCH-5

That on 01.04.2024 at about 7.00 p.m. petitioner was walking on let side of the road, near Kalyanapura Gate, Tumkur - Kunigal Road, Hebbur Hobli, Tumkur District, at that time, a rider of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-EJ-3139 came in a very high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, due to the impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Adithya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkuru,
wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

entities.text: Adithya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkuru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. Petitioner submitted that at the time of accident, he was aged about 55 years, running Hotel Business and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m. and due to this accident, he is not able to continue his work,
incurred loss of income and he is suffering from permanent SCCH-5 disability.

With regard to accident, case registered in crime No.72/2024 against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-EJ-3139 before the Hebbur Police Station.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner of the said offending motor cycle and respondent No.2 is insured are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, respondent No.1 has appeared through counsel and filed written statement and submitted that, he is owner of the bike bearing Reg. No.AP-06-EJ-3139 having valid insurance policy bearing No.0714003123P113136430 valid from 11.01.2024 to 10.01.2025.
It is pertinent to note here itself that the bike bearing Reg. No.AP-06-EJ-3139 is not involved in this case.
Respondent No.1 contended that, SCCH-5 compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared through counsel and filed written statement and denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Further submitted that, respondent No.2 has issued insurance policy to the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-EJ-3139 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of Narasimhamurthy B U vs Lokesh K S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23398916/
2 M.V.Act.

6. Based on above pleadings of the parties following issues are framed:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the SCCH-5 motor vehicle accident that occurred on 01.04.2024 at about 7.00 p.m. near Kalyanapura Gate, Kunigal Road, Hebbur Hobli, Tumkur due to rash and negligent driving of one motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-EJ-3139 and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and examined Dr.Ramesh,
Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-2, Manager in Medical Record Department at Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre as PW-3 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
On the other hand, respondents side not lead evidence.
SCCH-5 8.
Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9.
Issue No.1:- In order to prove the case, petitioner has examined as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the petition averments.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

The petitioner has produced and got marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of mahazar as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.6.
SCCH-5 10.
Further to substantiate the petitioner's case, he has examined Manager in Medical Record Department and Doctor as PW-2 and PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and Narasimhamurthy B U vs Lokesh K S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23398916/
3 documents i.e., FIR, complaint, mahazar, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the accident dated 01.04.2024 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.

entities.text: Narasimhamurthy B U vs Lokesh K S
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the cross examination of PW-1 nothing is elicited to discard about manner of accident mentioned in FIR and petition.

11. Per contra, though respondents have appeared before the court, they have neither lead evidence nor produced any documents on their behalf to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

As there is no of iota of evidence to discard the evidence of petitioner SCCH-5 about the injuries sustained in the accident occurred on 01.04.2024 at about 7.00 p.m. when he was walking on left side fo the road, near Kalyanapura Gate,
Tumkur - Kunigal Road, Hebbur Hobli, Tumkur District.
12.
The final report submitted by police about the road traffic accident occurred due to negligence of rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-EJ3139.
Under such circumstances, considering the evidence of the petitioner this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained Grade II compound fracture both bone left leg, for which, he underwent surgery in the form of closed reduction and internal fixation with interlocking nail.

To prove this fact petitioner furnished SCCH-5 copy of wound certificate marked as per Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as per Ex.P.8 issued by Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, wherein he underwent treatment as impatient from 01.04.2024 to 07.04.2024.

Further the petitioner has produced medical bills for Rs.86,311/- marked as Ex.P.9,
medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.10 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.11.
14.

Further the petitioner has examined Dr.Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-2 and got marked OPD book marked as per Ex.P.12 and X-ray Films marked as per Ex.P.13.
Further he has assessed permanent physical disability of 32% of left lower limb, which is 16% of whole body.
In cross- examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and deposed that, fractures are SCCH-5 united and with difficulty petitioner can do his work.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 6%, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. Petitioner has examined Manager, Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre as PW-3 and he has produced authorization letter marked as Ex.P.14, case sheet marked as Ex.P.15 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.16.
16.

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 55 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.7, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is SCCH-5 01.06.1964 and the alleged accident is occurred on 01.04.2024, accordingly relying on Ex.P.7 his age is considered about 60 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 9 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.
Narasimhamurthy B U vs Lokesh K S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23398916/
4 Delhi Transport Corporation and others.
17.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss SCCH-5 income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Therefore, the loss of future income is as under; 15,750/-x12x9x6% = Rs.1,02,060/-
18.

It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 01.04.2024 to 07.04.2024 i.e., for 6 days.
For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income.
As per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.15,750/- p.m.

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,150/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
SCCH-5 19.
Further the petitioner has got marked Ex.P.9 medical bills for Rs.86,311/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for his treatment.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for Rs.86,311/- under medical expenses.
20. Except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondent has filed written statement and denied entire case of the petitioner in his evidence are all not sufficient to disbelieve the version of the petitioner.
It is the respondents who have to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
21. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No.

Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 1,02,060-00 SCCH-5 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges
4. Medical Expenses 86,311-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00

Narasimhamurthy B U vs Lokesh K S on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23398916/
5 6.

Loss of income during laid up 3,150-00 period Total Rs.2,36,521-00 Rounded off to Rs.2,37,000/-
22.

Accordingly this Tribunal hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,37,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

23. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0714003123P113136430 which is valid for the period from 11.01.2024 to 10.01.2025, the alleged accident was occurred on 01.04.2024 it reveals that, as on the date of SCCH-5 accident, insurance policy was in force.
Hence respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
For these reasons Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,37,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Thirty Seven Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his SCCH-5 account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

2025) (SHARMILA KAMATH K.)

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,37,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Thirty Seven Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his SCCH-5 account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
